section: India - natural vegetation types and their distribution; forest cover (India State of Forest Report)
subsections: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank
Most widespread forest type and area ranking

accepted.s: The classification of Indian forest types associated with H.G. Champion and G.S. Puri comprises how many major types and sub-types?
accepted.x: The classification associated with H.G. Champion and G.S. Puri recognises 5 major types and 15 sub-types.
accepted.tq: Directly distinguish the paired numerical classification figures.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s: Which one of the following forest types is correctly matched with its characteristic rainfall?
o: Tropical wet evergreen — less than 25 cm
accepted.x: Tropical thorn forests occur in areas receiving about 25–75 cm of rainfall. Wet evergreen forests require more than 250 cm, semi-evergreen forests 200–250 cm, and dry deciduous forests 75–100 cm.
accepted.tq: Use the rainfall range to eliminate reversed forest-type pairs.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding tropical wet evergreen forests:
1. They generally occur in areas receiving more than 250 cm of rainfall.
2. They are found in parts of the Western Ghats and North-Eastern India.
3. They account for approximately 37% of India’s forest area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Tropical wet evergreen forests require more than 250 cm of rainfall and occur in the Western Ghats, Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, Nagaland and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Their share is about 8%, not 37%.
accepted.tq: Identify the false percentage while retaining the correct distribution statements.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s: Which of the following groups contains only important species of tropical wet evergreen forests in India?
accepted.x: Rosewood, ebony, mahogany, gurjan and ironwood are among the important species of tropical wet evergreen forests.
accepted.tq: Group species by the forest type in which they naturally occur.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s: Semi-evergreen forests in India are mainly found:
o: Only above the Himalayan tree line
In the driest parts of Rajasthan and Gujarat
Along the fringes of evergreen forest belts
accepted.x: Semi-evergreen forests occur along the fringes of evergreen belts and contain a mixture of evergreen and deciduous species.
accepted.tq: Test the location and mixed composition of a confusable forest category.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (Forest type)
a. Moist deciduous
b. Dry deciduous
c. Thorn

d. Littoral or tidal

List-II (Characteristic species)
i. Rhizophora and Avicennia
ii. Teak, sal and mahua
iii. Acacia, Ziziphus and Prosopis
iv. Teak, sandalwood and Terminalia

Codes:
accepted.x: Moist deciduous forests include teak, sal and mahua; dry deciduous forests include teak, sandalwood and Terminalia; thorn forests include Acacia, Ziziphus and Prosopis; tidal forests include Rhizophora and Avicennia.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure mangrove pair and complete the species associations.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s: The dry deciduous forests of Andhra Pradesh are particularly associated with:
o: The deltas of the Godavari and Krishna only
The Nallamala and Eastern Ghats regions
The tidal creeks of the Sundarbans
The high alpine meadows of the Himalaya
accepted.x: In Andhra Pradesh, dry deciduous forests are especially associated with the Nallamala and Eastern Ghats. Their characteristic species include teak, sandalwood, Terminalia and red sanders.
accepted.tq: Link the regional distribution with the correct forest formation.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Moist deciduous forest — only the Trans-Himalayan region
Tropical thorn forest — Rajasthan, Gujarat and Rayalaseema
Alpine forest — deltas and tidal creeks
Littoral forest — western Rajasthan and adjoining Punjab
accepted.x: Tropical thorn forests occur in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Rayalaseema and contain Acacia, Ziziphus, Prosopis, babul and cacti.
accepted.tq: Use location-based elimination for similar forest formations.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s: Shola forests are best described as:
o: Temperate forests of the Nilgiris, Anaimalai and Palani hills
Alpine meadows above the Himalayan tree line
Tropical thorn forests of the north-western plains
accepted.x: Sholas are temperate forest formations of the Nilgiris, Anaimalai and Palani hills, generally occurring as stunted evergreen patches with grasslands in the Western Ghats.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the regional meaning of the term ‘Shola’ from alpine and mangrove formations.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about alpine vegetation in India:
1. It occurs above the tree line in the Himalaya.
2. Alpine meadows may extend up to about 4,750 metres.
3. It is principally a tidal-coast formation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Alpine vegetation occurs above the tree line in the Himalaya, and alpine meadows may extend up to about 4,750 metres. It is not a tidal-coast formation.
accepted.tq: Reject the geographically incompatible statement.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s: The natural vegetation of areas receiving less than 25 cm of rainfall is predominantly:
o: Evergreen vegetation of Assam and Meghalaya
Mangrove vegetation of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Moist deciduous vegetation of Odisha and West Bengal
Xerophytic vegetation of western Rajasthan and adjoining Punjab and Gujarat
accepted.x: Desert vegetation occurs in areas receiving less than 25 cm of rainfall and is dominated by xerophytes in western Rajasthan and adjoining Punjab and Gujarat. Date palms occur in oases.
accepted.tq: Apply the rainfall threshold to identify the corresponding vegetation.
accepted.sec: Forest types → distribution and species

accepted.s: The India State of Forest Report is published at which interval by the Forest Survey of India?
accepted.x: The India State of Forest Report is a biennial publication of the Forest Survey of India under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
accepted.tq: Directly test the publication cycle and institutional authority.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: For the purpose of the India State of Forest Report, forest cover refers to land of more than one hectare having canopy density of at least:
accepted.x: Forest cover includes land exceeding one hectare with canopy density of 10% or more, regardless of ownership.
accepted.tq: Separate the area criterion from the canopy-density criterion.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the density classes used in the India State of Forest Report?
o: Very Dense Forest: 40% or more; Moderately Dense Forest: 20–40%; Open Forest: below 20%
Very Dense Forest: 80% or more; Moderately Dense Forest: 50–80%; Open Forest: 20–50%
Very Dense Forest: 60% or more; Moderately Dense Forest: 30–60%; Open Forest: 10–30%
Very Dense Forest: 70% or more; Moderately Dense Forest: 40–70%; Open Forest: 10–40%
accepted.x: The classes are Very Dense Forest at 70% or more, Moderately Dense Forest at 40–70%, and Open Forest at 10–40% canopy density.
accepted.tq: Compare the adjacent canopy-density ranges without reversing their order.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding scrub is correct?
o: Scrub has canopy density below 10% and is not counted as forest cover.
Scrub has canopy density between 40% and 70% and is counted as moderately dense forest.
Scrub has canopy density of 70% or more and is counted as very dense forest.
Scrub has canopy density between 10% and 40% and is counted as open forest.
accepted.x: Scrub is assigned to areas with canopy density below 10% and is excluded from the forest-cover category.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the lower threshold of scrub from the open-forest range.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: According to ISFR 2023, which of the following combinations is correct for India’s forest cover, tree cover and their combined extent?
o: Forest cover 25.17%, tree cover 3.41%, combined cover 28.58%
Forest cover 21.76%, tree cover 3.41%, combined cover 25.17%
Forest cover 24.62%, tree cover 2.14%, combined cover 26.76%
Forest cover 20.00%, tree cover 5.17%, combined cover 25.17%
accepted.x: ISFR 2023 reported forest cover of 7,15,343 sq km or 21.76%, tree cover of 1,12,014 sq km or 3.41%, and combined forest and tree cover of 25.17%.
accepted.tq: Match the three related percentages rather than treating them as interchangeable.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: The total forest and tree cover reported in ISFR 2023 was approximately:
accepted.x: ISFR 2023 reported 7,15,343 sq km of forest cover and 1,12,014 sq km of tree cover, together amounting to 8,27,357 sq km.
accepted.tq: Add the two component areas to identify the combined figure.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: What was the net gain in India’s forest and tree cover between 2021 and 2023 as reported in ISFR 2023?
accepted.x: The net gain in forest and tree cover between 2021 and 2023 was reported as 1,445.81 sq km.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the net gain from its separate forest-cover and tree-cover components.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the increase in green cover reported in ISFR 2023:
1. The total increase was about 1,445 sq km.
2. About 156 sq km of the increase was forest cover.
3. About 1,289 sq km was tree cover outside recorded forests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the total increase was about 1,445 sq km, including 156 sq km of forest cover and 1,289 sq km of tree cover outside recorded forests.
accepted.tq: Use the component figures to verify the aggregate increase.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: Which State had the third-largest forest cover in India according to the figures provided for ISFR 2023?
accepted.x: Chhattisgarh had the third-largest forest cover, measuring about 55,812 sq km. Odisha had about 61,204 sq km, while Meghalaya was notable for the share of its geographical area under forest.
accepted.tq: Separate ranking by absolute forest area from ranking by percentage of geographical area.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states Meghalaya’s position in relation to forest cover?
o: About 56% of its geographical area is under forest
About 36% of its geographical area is under forest
About 96% of its geographical area is under forest
About 76% of its geographical area is under forest
accepted.x: Approximately 76% of Meghalaya’s geographical area is under forest, according to the figures cited.
accepted.tq: Test percentage of geographical area rather than absolute forest-cover ranking.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: Which type of forest is considered most vulnerable to forest fires?
accepted.x: Dry deciduous forests are especially vulnerable to fires because of their seasonal dryness and accumulation of dry biomass.
accepted.tq: Associate fire vulnerability with the seasonally dry forest type.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s: With reference to forest fires during 2023–24, which one of the following is correct regarding Andhra Pradesh?
o: It had the smallest fire-affected area and ranked first in large-fire events.
It had the largest fire-affected area, about 5,286.76 sq km, and ranked third in large-fire events.
It ranked third in fire-affected area, with about 2,856.76 sq km affected.
It had the largest fire-affected area, but recorded no large-fire events.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh had the largest fire-affected area in 2023–24, measuring about 5,286.76 sq km, and ranked third in large-fire events.
accepted.tq: Check both the absolute area figure and the separate event ranking.
accepted.sec: India State of Forest Report - cover share, density classes, top states, fire, global rank

accepted.s:
Arrange the following forest types in descending order of their share in India’s forest area:
A. Tropical dry deciduous
B. Tropical wet evergreen
C. Tropical moist deciduous
accepted.x: Tropical moist deciduous forests account for about 37%, tropical dry deciduous forests about 28.6%, and tropical wet evergreen forests about 8%.
accepted.tq: Rank the categories by percentage before selecting the sequence.
accepted.sec: Most widespread forest type and area ranking

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is the correct area ranking of the three forest types listed below?
1. Tropical moist deciduous
2. Tropical dry deciduous
3. Tropical wet evergreen
accepted.x: Tropical moist deciduous forests have a share of about 37%, tropical dry deciduous forests 28.6%, and tropical wet evergreen forests about 8%.
accepted.tq: Match each forest type with its distinct share before comparing the ranking.
accepted.sec: Most widespread forest type and area ranking

accepted.s: The tropical deciduous forests of India together account for approximately what share of the country’s forest area?
accepted.x: Tropical moist deciduous and tropical dry deciduous forests together account for approximately 65.6% of India’s forest area.
accepted.tq: Add the two deciduous forest shares rather than selecting the larger individual category.
accepted.sec: Most widespread forest type and area ranking

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its Himalayan altitude zone?
accepted.x: Sub-tropical chir pine occurs around 1,000–1,800 metres. Moist temperate forests occur around 1,500–3,000 metres, alpine meadows around 2,900–6,000 metres, and dry alpine scrub above 4,000 metres.
accepted.tq: Match the vegetation zone with its altitude range without reversing the sequence.
accepted.sec: Most widespread forest type and area ranking

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Himalayan altitude zones:
1. Moist temperate forests include oak, deodar and fir.
2. Sub-alpine vegetation includes fir, birch and rhododendron.
3. Dry alpine scrub dominated by juniper occurs above about 4,000 metres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe Himalayan vegetation zones and their characteristic species or altitude.
accepted.tq: Verify each altitude-zone and species association separately.
accepted.sec: Most widespread forest type and area ranking

accepted.s: Tidal forests in India are found not only in deltaic and creek regions but also in the:
accepted.x: Tidal or mangrove forests occur in deltas and creeks and also in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
accepted.tq: Use the coastal-island association to identify the additional distribution area.
accepted.sec: Most widespread forest type and area ranking
